scene.head: with_body
scene.placeText: the open front of a little wooden cable car climbing an impossibly steep street of her steam city on a bright morning — polished brass poles and the long grip lever before her, riders on the running boards, bright-painted wooden houses on both sides and the misty bay with white sails far below
scene.ownProp: a long polished brass grip lever with a worn wooden handle
scene.outfit: a gripwoman look fitted to her body — a sleeveless waistcoat-corset panelled in honey-varnished wood with brass rail trim, high-waisted work shorts, one large brass gauntlet shaped like a grip lever, a small brass bell at her throat, a coil of braided steel cable at her hip and laced boots
scene.scene: she is the gripwoman of the cable car, standing at the grip with both hands on its polished brass lever to take hold of the humming cable beneath the street, ringing the bell as the car starts up the hill

prompt:

This is her world's own everyday life, not our present day: every made thing around her — tools, cups, lamps, signs, vehicles, money and devices — is made the way her world makes them.
Let the place itself carry this world through its materials, fittings and objects; do not add the city's landmarks, airships or a skyline unless the place below names them. Wherever the place below sounds sooty, smoky, grimy or rusty, show it clean and gleaming instead.
